title: On optimum recognition error and reject tradeoff
relevance: Origin of the reject option as an error-reject tradeoff; the framing in which abstention is a cost, which our task departs from.

title: On the Foundations of Noise-free Selective Classification
relevance: Names selective classification and the risk-coverage trade-off, the evaluation frame we contrast with.

title: Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 30 (NIPS 2017)
relevance: Selective classifier with a user-set risk level that rejects to meet it; abstention traded against coverage.

title: Know What You Don't Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD
relevance: Canonical unanswerable-QA benchmark where insufficiency is a property of a question against a passage, established by annotation.

title: Do Large Language Models Know What They Don't Know?
relevance: SelfAware: unanswerable questions in free text for measuring LLM self-knowledge; query-side insufficiency.

title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
relevance: Models can estimate whether they know an answer (P(IK)); bears on whether models can recognise unassessable pairs when allowed to say so.

title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
relevance: Survey organising LLM abstention by query, model and human values; situates our evidence-base insufficiency within that taxonomy.

title: AbstentionBench: Reasoning LLMs Fail on Unanswerable Questions
relevance: Large abstention benchmark over 20 datasets of unanswerable/underspecified questions; closest general-purpose abstention evaluation, query-side and free text.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
relevance: Defines context sufficiency and finds strong models answer incorrectly rather than abstain when context is insufficient; the closest analogue of our evidence-base insufficiency in RAG.

title: Why Language Models Hallucinate
relevance: Argues binary grading that gives no credit for expressing uncertainty rewards guessing; our schema ablation is an interface-level instance of the same incentive.

title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
relevance: Hallucination benchmark measuring falsehoods against world knowledge rather than against a supplied evidence base.

title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
relevance: Scores whether atomic claims are supported by a knowledge source; support-checking of generated text, not verdicts with an insufficiency class.

title: FEVER: a Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
relevance: Three-way Supported/Refuted/NotEnoughInfo labelling with annotated evidence; the nearest label structure to pass/fail/needs_evidence.

title: FEVEROUS: Fact Extraction and VERification Over Unstructured and Structured information
relevance: Extends supports/refutes/not-enough-info verification to table cells; annotated rather than constructed labels.

title: TabFact: A Large-scale Dataset for Table-based Fact Verification
relevance: Fact verification over tables with two labels (entailed/refuted) and no insufficiency class.

title: ClaimDB: A Fact Verification Benchmark over Large Structured Data
relevance: Claim verification over real multi-table databases with a not-enough-info class; reports that models struggle to abstain. Close to our structured-data-plus-abstention setting.

title: Spider: A Large-Scale Human-Labeled Dataset for Complex and Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing and Text-to-SQL Task
relevance: Standard text-to-SQL benchmark in which every question is answerable over the database.

title: EHRSQL: A Practical Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Electronic Health Records
relevance: Text-to-SQL over structured health records including unanswerable questions; a regulated-domain structured-records precedent for answerability.

title: Know What I don't Know: Handling Ambiguous and Unknown Questions for Text-to-SQL
relevance: Categorises ambiguous and unanswerable text-to-SQL questions and generates them counterfactually; insufficiency again a property of the question against a schema.

title: TrustSQL: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL Reliability with Penalty-Based Scoring
relevance: Benchmarks text-to-SQL reliability as answering feasible questions and abstaining on infeasible ones, under penalty-based scoring for incorrect output; the closest structured-data precedent for scoring abstention against wrong answers.

title: LegalBench: A Collaboratively Built Benchmark for Measuring Legal Reasoning in Large Language Models
verified_from: https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=2308.11462 (arXiv abstract record); venue from NeurIPS 2023 proceedings PDF URL returned by search
relevance: 162 expert-built legal reasoning tasks; evaluates reasoning over legal text, not evidence sufficiency over an organisation's records.

title: LexGLUE: A Benchmark Dataset for Legal Language Understanding in English
relevance: Standardised legal NLU benchmark over legal text classification tasks.

title: CUAD: An Expert-Annotated NLP Dataset for Legal Contract Review
relevance: Expert-annotated contract review (clause highlighting); illustrates the cost of expert annotation our construction avoids.

title: When Does Pretraining Help? Assessing Self-Supervised Learning for Law and the CaseHOLD Dataset
relevance: Multiple-choice case-holding identification; legal reasoning over case law.

title: LawBench: Benchmarking Legal Knowledge of Large Language Models
relevance: Legal knowledge memorisation, understanding and application tasks over legal text; text-side.

title: Large Legal Fictions: Profiling Legal Hallucinations in Large Language Models
relevance: Documents prevalent legal hallucination and that models do not always know when they hallucinate; motivates measuring unsupported legal outputs.

title: Hallucination-Free? Assessing the Reliability of Leading AI Legal Research Tools
relevance: Pre-registered evaluation showing commercial legal tools hallucinate despite vendor claims; precedent for testing deployed legal-AI claims and for pre-registration.

title: ImmigrationQA: A Source-Grounded Dataset and Small-Model Adaptation for U.S. Immigration Law
relevance: Question answering over US immigration policy sources; text-side, no employer records.

title: ImmigrationReason: A Structured Dataset of U.S. Immigration Appeals for Legal Reasoning Research
relevance: Structured dataset of USCIS AAO appeal decisions with per-criterion evidence-sufficiency findings and adjudicator-error quotes; closest immigration dataset, but labels extracted from adjudications, not employer records.

title: Semantic NLP-Based Information Extraction from Construction Regulatory Documents for Automated Compliance Checking
venue: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering 30(2)
relevance: Representative automated compliance checking work: extracting rules from regulatory text to check against project data.

title: Question Answering for Privacy Policies: Combining Computational and Legal Perspectives
relevance: PrivacyQA, with expert annotations and analysis of question answerability over privacy policies.

title: AI-enabled Automation for Completeness Checking of Privacy Policies
relevance: GDPR completeness checking of privacy policies: compliance assessment of a document against provisions, the closest pre-LLM compliance-checking task.

title: COMPL-AI Framework: A Technical Interpretation and LLM Benchmarking Suite for the EU Artificial Intelligence Act
relevance: Assesses whether LLMs comply with the EU AI Act; the AI system is the regulated subject, the inverse of our setting.

title: LLM-based HSE Compliance Assessment: Benchmark, Performance, and Advancements
relevance: HSE-Bench: LLMs assessing health-and-safety compliance via IRAC-structured questions; compliance assessment framed as question answering.

title: ReguSim: Evaluating LLM Agent Rule Grounding in Financial Compliance
relevance: Includes ReguBench, a target-marked monitoring benchmark judging records for rule violations; finds simple structured baselines match or exceed prompt-only LLMs. Close to our record-level verdict setting in finance.

title: A Four-Axis Trustworthiness Benchmark for LLM-as-Judge in Principle-Based Regulation
venue: KDD 2026 Workshop on Secure and Trustworthy LLMs (per arXiv comment); arXiv:2608.14329
relevance: LLM-as-judge compliance assessment of financial promotions under a pre-registered rubric; assessor-side, like ours, but over text against principles.

title: DEMM-Bench: A Cross-Regime Benchmark for Agent-Runtime Governance-Evidence Sufficiency
relevance: Measures whether agent-runtime records suffice to reconstruct decision properties, with an overclaim rate and construction-oracle labels; its "container fallacy" closely parallels our adjacent-field substitution.

title: Partial Evidence Bench: Benchmarking Authorization-Limited Evidence in Agentic Systems
relevance: Deterministic synthetic benchmark (including a compliance-audit family) scoring unsafe completeness when evidence lies outside an agent's view; the closest prior work to our false-green framing.

title: Datasheets for Datasets
relevance: Documentation standard our released datasheet follows.

title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
relevance: Reporting standard for models; precedent for our stated reporting requirement (false-green rate always beside recall).

title: Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks
relevance: Shows test-set label errors are common and can change model rankings; motivates our blind label audit and its reported effect on rankings.

title: NLP Evaluation in trouble: On the Need to Measure LLM Data Contamination for each Benchmark
relevance: Argues contamination must be measured per benchmark; the seeded generator lets fresh firms be drawn so a static test set need not be trusted.

title: Towards AI-Complete Question Answering: A Set of Prerequisite Toy Tasks
relevance: bAbI: synthetic tasks with answers fixed by the generator; precedent for ground truth by construction.

title: Let Me Speak Freely? A Study On The Impact Of Format Restrictions On Large Language Model Performance
relevance: Format restrictions on generation degrade LLM reasoning; related to, but distinct from, our ablation, which removes a label from the permitted set.

title: Political Compass or Spinning Arrow? Towards More Meaningful Evaluations for Values and Opinions in Large Language Models
relevance: Models give substantively different answers when forced into a multiple-choice format than when not forced; forced choice manufactures answers, as our withheld condition does.

title: Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design or: How I learned to start worrying about prompt formatting
relevance: Large performance swings from meaning-preserving prompt-format changes; caution for our single frozen prompt and reason to hold it fixed across conditions.
